title: Double hamburger on white bun, 2 large patties

content.title: About
content.content: The double hamburger consists of two large beef patties (about 100 g each), melted cheese, fresh lettuce, a slice of tomato, pickles, onion and sauce, placed between two halves of a soft white bun. A perfect balance of juicy meat and tender bread.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first double hamburger appeared in the United States in the 1970s as a response to growing demand for heartier meals.
White buns usually contain more sugar and fat than whole‑grain buns, making them softer and sweeter.
A 100 g patty provides roughly 250 kcal and 20 g of protein.
The combination of two patties and cheese raises the calcium content to about 150 mg per serving.
Hamburgers are often served with french fries and a soft drink, which doubles the overall calorie load.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Beef patties supply high‑quality protein essential for muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Source of iron
items.content: Red meat provides heme iron, which is more readily absorbed than plant‑based iron.

items.title: Contains vitamin B12
items.content: Vitamin B12 supports nervous system function and red blood cell formation.

items.title: Calcium from cheese
items.content: Melted cheese adds calcium, important for bone and teeth health.

items.title: Vegetable contribution
items.content: Tomato and lettuce add a modest amount of vitamin C and dietary fiber.

items.title: High calorie content
items.content: A double hamburger can contain 700–800 kcal, which may contribute to weight gain if eaten frequently.

items.title: Saturated fat and sodium
items.content: The burger contains notable amounts of saturated fat and salt, which can raise cholesterol and blood pressure.

items.title: Dairy allergy
items.content: Cheese may trigger reactions in people with lactose intolerance or milk protein allergy.

items.title: Additives
items.content: Some pre‑made patties may contain additives such as monosodium glutamate, which can cause sensitivity in certain individuals.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the burger hot, split the bun, and place all ingredients inside. It is traditionally eaten with the hands, though a knife and fork can be used if preferred. Add mustard, ketchup, or mayo to taste.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Prepared burgers are best consumed immediately. If needed, store in the refrigerator for up to 24 hours in an airtight container. Reheat in an oven or skillet rather than a microwave to retain bun texture.
